The radar defending a city, the cables carrying your internet... both need metals one country controls!
China. It makes ninety-nine percent of the world's gallium.
It's in power chips, LED lights, and the radars of modern air defence. Its cousin germanium carries light through fibre-optic cables.
In twenty twenty-three, China put both under licence. In December twenty twenty-four, it banned exports to America outright.
Gallium more than doubled in Europe. Germanium hit about five thousand dollars a kilo, five times its early twenty twenty-three price.
After a Trump-Xi truce, the ban on America was paused... for now.
